title: Executive Interview with Victor Lopez of RaiderChip
gist: RaiderChip CTO Victor Lopez presents a European fabless startup (founded 2024) building a Transformer-inference NPU for edge Generative AI, sold as chips and licensable IP, with first silicon (Kairós) heading to tape-out and an FPGA prototype supporting 50+ models. He pitches technological sovereignty and Physical AI as demand drivers.

themes.theme: Edge generative AI flexibility versus efficiency

insights.claim: Edge Generative AI faces a trade-off: general-purpose processors are flexible but inefficient, while conventional NPUs are efficient but struggle with new GenAI architectures, causing limited model ecosystems, conversion needs and precision constraints.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The flexibility-versus-efficiency gap is the opening for new edge NPU architectures.
insights.quote: The industry has yet to fully resolve the fundamental trade-off
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: RaiderChip claims specialized hardware kernels covering all fundamental Transformer operations, a deterministic-latency pipeline, firmware-defined model-specific execution and a hardware scheduler across tensor, vector and memory units give custom-like efficiency without redesigning silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Model-by-model scheduling is how it hopes to future-proof against evolving models.
insights.locator: The key to our flexibility and efficiency

insights.claim: Running supported workloads entirely on one NPU avoids splitting across CPUs, GPUs and accelerators, cutting data transfers and integration complexity and avoiding hardware overprovisioning, which improves power, area and cost.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Single-engine execution is a cost-competitiveness argument for edge SoCs.
insights.locator: Furthermore, by executing supported Generative AI workloads

insights.claim: Lopez believes Generative AI may become a general-purpose technology across virtually every sector, motivating a scalable architecture tailored to different performance, power and cost points.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A broad-market framing for an edge IP licensing play.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: RaiderChip sees robotics, automotive and industrial automation as strongest areas, where AI must interact with the physical world under strict power, latency and autonomy constraints, driving the transition toward Physical AI.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Edge NPU demand is tied to physical-AI deployment timing.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Lopez believes the future of Physical AI lies in combining multiple specialized models, requiring native support for fine-tuned and post-trained models and concurrent execution of multiple GenAI models.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hardware must host model ensembles, not a single model, at the edge.
insights.quote: We believe the future of Physical AI lies in combining multiple specialized models working together.
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

insights.claim: A robotics demo ran ten models, including speech recognition, a four-billion-parameter reasoning model and robotic control policies, concurrently on a single FPGA-based Kairós NPU prototype locally with no cloud, with robots simulated in Google DeepMind's MuJoCo.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows multi-model edge inference is feasible on a small prototype, though simulated robots.

insights.claim: Customers worry about technological sovereignty and dependence on a few international suppliers of advanced technologies, since recent geopolitical tensions and export restrictions on advanced hardware have shown how concentration can jeopardize autonomy and continuity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: European demand for domestic AI silicon is a tailwind for local startups.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Edge product makers must decide today which performance levels, models and architectures to support over a product lifecycle, because no established GenAI roadmaps exist and models evolve rapidly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Roadmap uncertainty favors flexible architectures and licensable IP.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: RaiderChip, a European fabless company founded in 2024, combines chip development with licensing its NPU as IP for third-party SoCs, and is moving toward tape-out of its first-generation chip Kairós.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pre-silicon, so execution and tape-out risk remain.
insights.quote: We are currently moving towards the tape-out of Kairós
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?

insights.claim: The FPGA-based NPU prototype supports more than 50 models and is available for evaluation under NDA, with modular, scalable IP tailored to each application's performance, power and area.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Evaluation traction is the early commercial signal to watch.
